close_reason: Bead is opinion-adjacent (bead author flagged 'low-stakes — flag as an opinion-adjacent stylistic note'). Kept the #[non_exhaustive] attribute on RequestError because (a) it documents forward-compat intent at the type-definition site, (b) a future pub field then does not need to add the attribute as a separate change. Added a comment explaining the rationale so a future reader doesn't re-litigate the same bikeshed.
description: src/response.rs:84-89 declares 'pub struct RequestError' with #[non_exhaustive] but both fields ('status: StatusCode' and 'err: JmapError') are private. #[non_exhaustive] on a struct prevents (a) outside-crate struct-literal construction and (b) exhaustive pattern matching from outside the crate. Private fields already prevent both — there is no way to construct or destructure a struct with all-private fields from another crate to begin with. The attribute is functionally a no-op here. Idiomatic Rust uses #[non_exhaustive] when at least one field is pub (where it does protect against breaking changes from adding more pub fields), or omits it when all fields are private. Defensible counter-argument: 'leaves the door open for a future field to be pub without further consideration', and the attribute documents intent. Low-stakes — flag as an opinion-adjacent stylistic note. What goes wrong if it stays: very little; a future reader may wonder why the attribute is there when the privacy already prevents the same outcomes.
title: RequestError is #[non_exhaustive] but all fields are private — the attribute is largely redundant
